description: 生物医学检索评测集 — 60 篇语料 / 40 条带标注查询

corpus.title: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells targeting CD19 in refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
corpus.abstract: Autologous T cells engineered to express a CD19-specific chimeric antigen receptor induced durable remission in patients with refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

corpus.title: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
corpus.abstract: CD19-directed CAR T cells produced high response rates in relapsed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, though cytokine release syndrome remains a common toxicity.

corpus.title: Cytokine release syndrome following CAR T-cell infusion
corpus.abstract: Cytokine release syndrome is a frequent and potentially life-threatening complication of CAR T-cell therapy, driven by massive T-cell activation and release of inflammatory cytokines.

corpus.title: Overcoming barriers to CAR T-cell therapy in solid tumors
corpus.abstract: Unlike hematologic malignancies, solid tumors resist CAR T-cell therapy because of antigen heterogeneity, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and poor T-cell trafficking.

corpus.title: CD19 antigen loss as a mechanism of CAR T-cell resistance
corpus.abstract: Relapse after anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is frequently associated with loss of CD19 expression on malignant B cells, an immune escape mechanism.

corpus.title: Engineering next-generation CARs with dual costimulation
corpus.abstract: Second and third generation CAR constructs incorporate costimulatory domains such as CD28 and 4-1BB to enhance T-cell persistence and effector function.

corpus.title: Lipid nanoparticle delivery of mRNA vaccines against SARS-CoV-2
corpus.abstract: mRNA vaccines encapsulate the spike protein coding sequence inside lipid nanoparticles, which protect the RNA and enable intracellular delivery to antigen-presenting cells.

corpus.title: Efficacy of the mRNA-1273 vaccine against symptomatic COVID-19
corpus.abstract: The mRNA-1273 vaccine demonstrated roughly 94 percent efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19 in a large randomized placebo-controlled trial.

corpus.title: mRNA vaccine platform from cancer immunotherapy to infectious disease
corpus.abstract: The same mRNA platform originally developed for cancer immunotherapy was rapidly repurposed to encode viral antigens, enabling fast vaccine design.

corpus.title: Rare adverse events after mRNA COVID-19 vaccination
corpus.abstract: mRNA COVID-19 vaccines are associated with rare adverse events including myocarditis in younger males, which must be weighed against the risks of infection.

corpus.title: Booster doses and waning immunity after mRNA vaccination
corpus.abstract: Neutralizing antibody titers decline over months after primary mRNA vaccination, and booster doses restore protection against severe disease.

corpus.title: Stability and cold-chain requirements of mRNA vaccines
corpus.abstract: mRNA vaccines are inherently unstable and require ultra-cold storage, prompting research into lyophilized and thermostable formulations.

corpus.title: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in mammalian cells
corpus.abstract: The CRISPR-Cas9 system uses a guide RNA to direct the Cas9 nuclease to a complementary DNA sequence, producing a targeted double-strand break that enables gene editing.

corpus.title: Off-target effects of CRISPR-Cas9
corpus.abstract: Cas9 can cleave sequences that partially match the guide RNA, causing unintended off-target mutations that must be detected and minimized for safe editing.

corpus.title: Delivery of CRISPR components using adeno-associated virus
corpus.abstract: Adeno-associated virus vectors can deliver Cas9 and guide RNA to target tissues in vivo, though packaging limits and immunogenicity remain challenges.

corpus.title: CRISPR base editing for single-nucleotide correction
corpus.abstract: Base editors fuse a catalytically impaired Cas9 to a deaminase enzyme to convert one DNA base into another without creating a double-strand break.

corpus.title: Ethical considerations in human germline editing
corpus.abstract: Editing human embryos raises profound ethical questions about heritable genetic modification, consent, and equity, prompting calls for international governance.

corpus.title: CRISPR screens for functional genomics
corpus.abstract: Pooled CRISPR knockout and activation screens systematically perturb thousands of genes in parallel to reveal their roles in biological processes.

corpus.title: Amyloid-beta plaques in Alzheimer's disease pathology
corpus.abstract: Extracellular accumulation of amyloid-beta peptides into plaques is a defining pathological hallmark of Alzheimer's disease and a focus of diagnostic and therapeutic targeting.

corpus.title: Tau protein hyperphosphorylation and neurofibrillary tangles
corpus.abstract: Hyperphosphorylated tau protein aggregates into intracellular neurofibrillary tangles, which correlate more closely with cognitive decline than amyloid plaques.

corpus.title: Anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies for Alzheimer's therapy
corpus.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies that clear amyloid-beta plaques have shown modest slowing of cognitive decline in early Alzheimer's disease trials.

corpus.title: APOE4 as a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease
corpus.abstract: The apolipoprotein E epsilon4 allele is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, influencing amyloid clearance and neuroinflammation.

corpus.title: Biomarkers for early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease
corpus.abstract: Cerebrospinal fluid and blood biomarkers such as phosphorylated tau and amyloid ratio enable detection of Alzheimer's pathology years before clinical symptoms.

corpus.title: Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease progression
corpus.abstract: Chronic activation of microglia and astrocytes contributes to synapse loss and neurodegeneration, positioning neuroinflammation as a therapeutic target.

corpus.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes
corpus.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists enhance glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppress glucagon, improving glycemic control in type 2 diabetes.

corpus.title: Insulin resistance and beta-cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes
corpus.abstract: Type 2 diabetes arises from peripheral insulin resistance combined with progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction and relative insulin deficiency.

corpus.title: Cardiovascular benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists
corpus.abstract: Several GLP-1 receptor agonists have demonstrated reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk.

corpus.title: SGLT2 inhibitors and renal outcomes in diabetes
corpus.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors lower glucose and reduce the progression of diabetic kidney disease through hemodynamic and metabolic effects.

corpus.title: Metformin mechanism of action in type 2 diabetes
corpus.abstract: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity, remaining first-line therapy for type 2 diabetes.

corpus.title: Weight loss effects of semaglutide
corpus.abstract: Semaglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, produces substantial and sustained weight loss in patients with obesity and overweight.

corpus.title: Mechanisms of beta-lactam resistance in MRSA
corpus.abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus resists beta-lactam antibiotics through acquisition of the mecA gene encoding an altered penicillin-binding protein.

corpus.title: Emergence of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae
corpus.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae produce carbapenemase enzymes that hydrolyze last-resort antibiotics, posing a severe public health threat.

corpus.title: Efflux pumps and multidrug resistance
corpus.abstract: Bacterial efflux pumps actively expel multiple classes of antibiotics from the cell, contributing to multidrug resistance in many pathogens.

corpus.title: Antibiotic stewardship programs to curb resistance
corpus.abstract: Antimicrobial stewardship programs optimize antibiotic prescribing to slow the emergence of resistance and improve patient outcomes.

corpus.title: Horizontal gene transfer of antibiotic resistance genes
corpus.abstract: Resistance genes spread between bacteria through plasmids and transposons, accelerating the global dissemination of antibiotic resistance.

corpus.title: Phage therapy as an alternative to antibiotics
corpus.abstract: Bacteriophages specifically infect and kill bacteria, offering a potential alternative for treating multidrug-resistant infections.

corpus.title: PD-1 blockade in metastatic melanoma
corpus.abstract: Antibodies blocking the programmed cell death protein 1 receptor produce durable responses and improved survival in metastatic melanoma.

corpus.title: CTLA-4 inhibition and immune checkpoint blockade
corpus.abstract: Targeting cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 releases a brake on T-cell activation, forming the basis of early checkpoint inhibitor therapy.

corpus.title: Immune-related adverse events of checkpoint inhibitors
corpus.abstract: Checkpoint inhibitors can trigger immune-related adverse events such as colitis, pneumonitis, and endocrinopathies due to loss of peripheral tolerance.

corpus.title: Biomarkers predicting response to PD-1 therapy
corpus.abstract: PD-L1 expression, tumor mutational burden, and immune infiltration are candidate biomarkers for selecting patients likely to respond to checkpoint blockade.

corpus.title: Combination of checkpoint inhibitors with chemotherapy
corpus.abstract: Combining checkpoint blockade with chemotherapy can improve response rates by enhancing tumor antigen release and immune activation.

corpus.title: Tumor mutational burden and immunotherapy response
corpus.abstract: High tumor mutational burden correlates with increased neoantigen load and improved response to checkpoint inhibitors across several cancers.

corpus.title: Alpha-synuclein aggregation in Parkinson's disease
corpus.abstract: Misfolded alpha-synuclein aggregates into Lewy bodies in dopaminergic neurons, a central pathological feature of Parkinson's disease.

corpus.title: Deep brain stimulation for advanced Parkinson's disease
corpus.abstract: High-frequency electrical stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus improves motor symptoms in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease.

corpus.title: Dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra
corpus.abstract: Progressive degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta underlies the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease.

corpus.title: LRRK2 mutations and familial Parkinson's disease
corpus.abstract: Mutations in the leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 gene are the most common genetic cause of familial and sporadic Parkinson's disease.

corpus.title: Gut-brain axis in Parkinson's disease
corpus.abstract: Emerging evidence links gut microbiota and intestinal inflammation to the initiation of alpha-synuclein pathology and Parkinson's disease progression.

corpus.title: Neuroprotective strategies in Parkinson's disease
corpus.abstract: Neuroprotective approaches aim to slow dopaminergic degeneration through antioxidants, anti-inflammatory agents, and targeted molecular therapies.

corpus.title: Statins reduce LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular events
corpus.abstract: Statin therapy lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and reduces the incidence of myocardial infarction and stroke in at-risk patients.

corpus.title: PCSK9 inhibitors for familial hypercholesterolemia
corpus.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against PCSK9 dramatically lower LDL cholesterol in patients with familial hypercholesterolemia who are intolerant of statins.

corpus.title: Atherosclerosis and the role of inflammation
corpus.abstract: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the arterial wall in which lipid deposition and immune cell infiltration drive plaque formation.

corpus.title: Blood pressure control and stroke prevention
corpus.abstract: Lowering elevated blood pressure is the single most effective intervention for preventing stroke and other cardiovascular events.

corpus.title: Triglycerides and residual cardiovascular risk
corpus.abstract: Elevated triglycerides contribute to residual cardiovascular risk even after LDL cholesterol is controlled with statin therapy.

corpus.title: Aspirin in primary prevention of cardiovascular disease
corpus.abstract: Low-dose aspirin modestly reduces cardiovascular events in primary prevention but increases bleeding risk, limiting its net benefit.

corpus.title: Adeno-associated virus vectors for retinal gene therapy
corpus.abstract: AAV vectors delivered by subretinal injection restore vision in inherited retinal dystrophies such as RPE65-associated Leber congenital amaurosis.

corpus.title: AAV-mediated gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy
corpus.abstract: Intravenous AAV9 delivering the SMN1 gene improves motor function and survival in infants with spinal muscular atrophy.

corpus.title: Immune responses to AAV capsid
corpus.abstract: Pre-existing neutralizing antibodies against the AAV capsid and capsid-specific T-cell responses can limit transgene expression and durability.

corpus.title: Hemophilia B gene therapy with factor IX
corpus.abstract: AAV-based gene therapy delivering factor IX achieves sustained factor expression and reduces bleeding in hemophilia B patients.

corpus.title: In vivo genome editing with AAV-delivered CRISPR
corpus.abstract: AAV vectors can co-deliver Cas9 and guide RNA to perform in vivo genome editing in the liver and other organs.

corpus.title: Manufacturing challenges for AAV gene therapy vectors
corpus.abstract: Producing high-titer, high-purity AAV vectors at scale remains a major cost and quality bottleneck for gene therapy.
